sections.heading: Part I — Student-Produced Response Questions (SPRs): Foundational Fluency (1–7)

questions.q: When reviewing field logs of commercial ceramic firing chambers collected while documenting yield ratios, tabulated frequencies above record \(10\) experimental outcomes; evaluate the mean reading.
questions.answer: **Answer:** \(14\). **Algebraic Method:** Weighted sum \(140\) divided by 10 yields \(14\). **Desmos Strategy:** Evaluate `mean([...])` in Desmos. **Trap Watchout:** Weight each value by its frequency.

questions.q: Consider this precision hydroponic vertical racks projection profile gathered while calibrating telemetry instruments. Namely, at coordinate \(x = 4\), compute the absolute deviation separating observed data from \(y = 2x + 5\).
questions.answer: **Answer:** \(1\). **Algebraic Method:** Line gives \(13\) while dot stands at \(12\), residual \(1\). **Desmos Strategy:** Evaluate `abs(12 - (2*4 + 5))`. **Trap Watchout:** Report the residual magnitude rather than the y-value itself.

sections.heading: Part II — Multiple-Choice Questions (MCQs): Foundational Fluency (21–28)

questions.q: A recipe that serves \(6\) people calls for \(10\) cups of flour. How many cups of flour are needed to serve \(19\) people?
questions.answer: \(\frac{10}{6}=\frac{x}{19} \Rightarrow x=\frac{10\times 19}{6}=95/3\) cups.

questions.q: A jacket originally priced at 60 dollars is on sale for 20% off. What is the discount amount in dollars?
questions.answer: **Answer:** C. Discount = \( 0.20 \times 60 = 12 dollars \).

questions.q: If \( x \) is directly proportional to \( y \), and \( x = 14 \) when \( y = 2 \), what is \( x \) when \( y = 5 \)?
questions.answer: **Answer:** D. Constant of proportionality \( k = x/y = 14/2 = 7 \). When \( y = 5 \), \( x = 7 \times 5 = 35 \).

questions.q: A recipe requires 2 cups of sugar for every 3 cups of flour. If 9 cups of flour are used, how many cups of sugar are needed?
questions.answer: \(\frac{2}{3} = \frac{s}{9} \implies s = 6\) cups of sugar.

questions.q: A survey found that 3 out of every 8 households own a pet. In a neighborhood of 640 households, how many are expected to own a pet?
questions.answer: **Answer:** D. \( \dfrac{3}{8} \times 640 = 3 \times 80 = 240 \).

questions.q: If \(x\) is directly proportional to \(y\), and \(x = 14\) when \(y = 2\), what is \(x\) when \(y = 5\)?
questions.answer: Constant of proportionality \(k = x/y = 14/2 = 7\). When \(y = 5\), \(x = 7 \times 5 = 35\).

questions.q: A store buys backpacks for \(40\) dollars and marks them up by \(35\%\). What is the selling price?
questions.answer: **Answer:** \(54\) dollars. \(40 \times 1.35 = 54\) dollars.

questions.q: In a recipe, \(3\) cups of oats serve \(5\) people. How many cups of oats are needed for \(35\) people?
questions.answer: **Answer:** \(21\). Multiply \(3 \times (35 / 5) = 21\) cups.

sections.heading: Part II — Multiple-Choice Questions (MCQs): Intermediate Application (29–37)

questions.q: The scatter plot shows the relationship between study hours and scores. Which best describes the correlation?
questions.answer: As study hours increase, scores consistently increase. The points follow a clear upward trend — strong positive correlation.

questions.q: A printer prints 45 pages in 3 minutes. At this rate, how many pages can it print in 8 minutes?
questions.answer: **Answer:** D. Rate = \( 45 / 3 = 15 \) pages per minute. In 8 minutes: \( 15 \times 8 = 120 \) pages.

questions.q: A cyclist travels at a constant speed of 12 miles per hour. How many miles does the cyclist travel in 3.5 hours?
questions.answer: \(\text{Distance} = \text{speed} \times \text{time} = 12 \times 3.5 = 42\) miles.

questions.q: A class of 30 students has 18 girls and 12 boys. What percentage of the class is boys?
If a team won 21 games and lost 7 games, what fraction of their games did they win?
questions.answer: **Answer:** C. Total games = \( 21 + 7 = 28 \). Fraction won = \( 21 / 28 = 3/4 \).

questions.q: Population rises from \(16,000\) to \(20,000\) over five years. By what percentage did the population grow?
A line of best fit for electricity bills versus home area (in square feet) is \(\hat{y} = 0.08x + 42\). What does \(0.08\) represent?
choices: Predicted dollar increase per additional square foot
questions.answer: **Answer:** Predicted dollar increase per additional square foot. The slope \(0.08\) gives the predicted change in \(\hat{y}\) (dollars) per \(1\) unit increase in \(x\) (sq ft).

questions.q: How many square inches are in a \(3\)-foot by \(4\)-foot poster (\(1\text{ foot} = 12\text{ inches}\))?
questions.answer: **Answer:** \(1,728\). \(36\text{ in} \times 48\text{ in} = 1,728\text{ in}^2\).

questions.q: A hybrid sedan travels \(48\) miles per gallon in city traffic. How many gallons of fuel are consumed on a \(216\)-mile trip at that efficiency?

sections.heading: Part II — Multiple-Choice Questions (MCQs): Challenging Synthesis (38–45)

questions.q: An item's price increased from 50 dollars to 65 dollars. What was the percent increase?
questions.answer: Percent increase = \(\frac{65 - 50}{50} \times 100\% = \frac{15}{50} \times 100\% = 30\%\).

questions.q: A runner completes a 5-kilometer race in 25 minutes. What is the runner's average speed in kilometers per hour?
questions.answer: 25 minutes is \(25/60 = 5/12\) hours. Speed \(= 5 / (5/12) = 12 \text{ km/h}\).

questions.q: An electronic device is discounted from 200 dollars to 160 dollars. What is the percent discount?
If 6 workers take 8 days to complete a job, how many days would 12 workers take working at the same pace?
questions.answer: **Answer:** B. Total worker-days = \( 6 \times 8 = 48 \). With 12 workers: \( 48 / 12 = 4 \) days.

questions.q: If \(\frac{a}{15} = \frac{4}{5}\), what is the value of \(a\)?
A store sells notebooks in packs of 5 for 6 dollars. How much would 25 notebooks cost at this rate?
questions.answer: 25 notebooks is 5 packs: 5 dollars \times 6 dollars = 30 dollars$.

questions.q: A price increases by \(20\%\) and is later decreased by \(20\%\). Compared with the starting price, the final price is:
questions.answer: **Answer:** \(4\%\) lower. \(1.20 \times 0.80 = 0.96\), which is \(4\%\) below the starting price.

questions.q: If \(p\) is \(25\%\) greater than \(q\), and \(q\) is \(20\%\) less than \(r\), how does \(p\) compare to \(r\)?
